reason: The submitted classification, (d) inverse hexagonal, agrees with the source diagrams and established cardiolipin phase behavior. The Lean derivation is logically valid and nonvacuous, but proves only curvature-sign compatibility under a candidate-defined qualitative packing model, not that actual fully protonated PL1 physically forms that phase. Thus the formal result is additionally conditioned.

coverage.evidence: PDF page 46 and T5_page-3.png ask for the fully protonated phase and map option (d) to the inverse-hexagonal diagram. The proof derives negative model curvature after protonation and proves that only choice d has that curvature. However, PhaseFits is defined merely as curvature-sign equality and is not connected by a proved physical law to actual phase formation.

unsupported_assumptions: Matching a phase diagram's three-valued curvature sign is treated as necessary and sufficient for physical phase formation.
Lamellar behavior is modeled as exact equality of effective head and hydrophobic areas, while any strictly smaller head area is taken to select the inverse-hexagonal phase.
A linear, strictly positive charge-expansion model is assumed to represent PL1; the qualitative charge trend is supported, but no actual PL1 model instance or bridge theorem is established.

Reduced cardiolipin headgroup charge favoring negative curvature is also supported by [Dahlberg](https://doi.org/10.1021/jp071954f).
